players.product: high-speed connectors & cable assemblies for AI racks

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q3 2026 sales were $5.2 billion, up 14% reported and 12% organic year over year. Adjusted EPS was a record $2.94, up 22%, with adjusted operating margin expanding 90 basis points to 21.9% and adjusted operating income above $1.1 billion. GAAP EPS was $2.55. CEO Terrence Curtin framed the quarter around TE sitting 'at the intersection of the largest technology and infrastructure investment cycle that's taking place around the world.'
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 sales $5.2B (+14% reported, +12% organic); adjusted EPS $2.94 (+22%); adjusted operating margin 21.9% (+90bps)

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q4 2026 guidance: sales of approximately $5.25 billion (+11% year over year) and adjusted EPS of approximately $3.05. For the full fiscal year TE now expects sales growth of approximately 15% - more than $2.5 billion of incremental revenue in 2026 - with adjusted EPS growth of 23%. Adjusted effective tax rate 23% in Q3, guided to 22-23% in Q4.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 FY2026 guide ~$5.25B (+11% YoY), adjusted EPS ~$3.05; FY2026 sales +15%, adjusted EPS +23%

quarterly_data.signal: Record orders of $5.7 billion, up 27% year over year (an increase of more than $1 billion) and 7% sequentially, with double-digit order growth in EVERY business across both segments and a book-to-bill of 1.1 both in the quarter and year to date. Industrial segment orders rose 36% year over year (about $800 million of the increase, roughly half of it from Digital Data Networks); Transportation orders rose 19% (about $400 million). Year to date, DDN orders are up over 70%, with energy, Aerospace & Defense and Automation & Connected Living all up 20%. The result is a record backlog position in both segments that management calls a strong growth indicator into fiscal 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: Record orders $5.7B (+27% YoY, +7% QoQ); book-to-bill 1.1; DDN orders +70% YTD; record backlog

quarterly_data.signal: Digital Data Networks (DDN) sales grew 34% year over year and rose $100 million sequentially, in line with expectations, and DDN is guided up again sequentially in Q4. AI as a percentage of DDN keeps climbing every quarter from the ~70% cited a few quarters ago. On the AI cloud target laid out at the late-2025 Investor Day - $3 billion in two years - Curtin said TE is already ahead of it and that the timeline 'continues to shift left,' so TE will be above $3 billion, with DDN a very big growth driver again in 2027. Management noted the AI-cloud versus enterprise split is blurring: the same agentic-CPU content counts as AI cloud when a hyperscaler buys it and enterprise when a server buyer does, which is why TE will report at the DDN level going forward.
quarterly_data.figure: DDN sales +34% YoY, +$100M QoQ; AI cloud $3B two-year target shifting left and will be exceeded

quarterly_data.signal: Copper versus optical: management insists it is 'copper AND optical.' Copper stays the workhorse inside the rack and in scale-up, and the shift to agentic workloads deploys MORE CPUs and networking, which increases the addressable market for high-speed copper connectivity. Scale-out is already almost entirely optical and TE openly states it has only a limited position there. The inflection management sees as incremental upside is CPO arriving at the switch level, which is where TE's fiber-array-unit technology plugs into its connectivity suite as incremental TAM rather than a substitution risk.

Optical roadmap via the RAM Photonics acquisition: TE added fiber-attached connectivity (FAU, fiber array unit) capability and says customer engagement around it is strong, opening incremental market access as optics move off the switch in scale-out architectures. Management was explicit on timing - 'you won't really see meaningful revenue until we get to 2028 and beyond' - and is currently investing in scaling both the manufacturing and the engineering teams from that acquisition to hit the customer intercept point in the 2028+ timeframe.
quarterly_data.figure: FAU/optical meaningful revenue not until 2028 and beyond

quarterly_data.signal: Power connectivity is roughly ONE THIRD of TE's AI revenue, with data connectivity the other two thirds. As customers move to higher-voltage rack architectures (some experimenting with 800V, though management sees a continuum of trade-offs rather than one end game), TE says content can rise to about 1.5x traditional power content. Curtin does not expect new entrants, because the rack is 'a simultaneous equation of trade-offs and constraints between the data and the power equation' and customers value a supplier that understands both the power chain and the signal chain. Introducing optics itself creates more power need.
quarterly_data.figure: ~1/3 of AI revenue is power connectivity; higher-voltage architectures worth ~1.5x traditional power content

quarterly_data.signal: Energy business organic sales grew 33%, contributing well over $100 million of the quarter's roughly $600 million of total growth. The business splits into roughly two thirds utilities/grid hardening (aging-infrastructure modernization), about 20% industrial - which is where TE brings power INTO the data center and into buildings, and is growing very fast - and the remainder clean energy. Management estimates about one third of the energy market growth where TE is positioned is driven by data center build-outs, and now frames energy as a mid-teens grower this year and next.
quarterly_data.figure: Energy organic sales +33%; >$100M of ~$600M total growth; ~1/3 of energy growth driven by data center build-outs

quarterly_data.signal: TE signed an agreement to acquire Astrodyne TDI for approximately $1.4 billion in cash, a bolt-on for the Industrial segment generating more than $250 million in annual sales, expected to close by the end of calendar 2026. About 40% of Astrodyne is power filtering (adding to TE's legacy position and the earlier Schaffner deal); the rest is custom power supplies going into SEMICONDUCTOR EQUIPMENT, defense and medical applications - management called out the semiconductor-equipment position as a direct beneficiary of AI-driven chip capacity additions. The deal is expected to be accretive to both growth and margins.
quarterly_data.figure: Astrodyne TDI: ~$1.4B purchase price, >$250M annual sales, closing end of calendar 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Cash generation: cash from operations was $1.2 billion in the quarter and free cash flow $883 million. Year to date free cash flow was roughly $2.2 billion and approximately $2 billion has been returned to shareholders through dividends and buybacks, with free cash flow conversion expected at roughly 100% for the year. GAAP operating income of $981 million included $9 million acquisition-related, $83 million restructuring and other, and $56 million amortization; full-year restructuring is still expected around $100 million.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 CFO $1.2B; Q3 FCF $883M; YTD FCF ~$2.2B; ~$2B returned YTD; ~100% FCF conversion

quarterly_data.signal: Transportation Solutions grew 7% reported and 5% organic with a 21% adjusted operating margin. Automotive rose 5% reported / 3% organic against slightly declining global vehicle production, with content outperformance held at the 4-6 point range; China sales grew 6% against production down 2% (eight points of outperformance) as OEM exports offset the weak domestic market, and Europe delivered four points of outperformance. Commercial Transportation grew 20% reported / 18% organic. Industrial Solutions grew 22% reported / 21% organic with adjusted operating margin up 70 basis points to nearly 23%, led by over 30% organic growth in both DDN and energy; Automation & Connected Living grew 16% / 14% and Aerospace & Defense 12%, with defense now growing faster than commercial aerospace.
quarterly_data.figure: Transportation +7% reported (21% margin); Industrial +22% reported (~23% margin); auto content outperformance 4-6 pts
